title: What is Elastic Beanstalk
description: Understand Elastic Beanstalk environments, application versions, and how ASP.NET Core apps run on AWS.

data.text: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a managed service for deploying and scaling web applications. You upload your ASP.NET Core binaries, and Elastic Beanstalk handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, and scaling automatically.

data.title: Key concepts
items: **Application** — a logical container for your project
**Environment** — a running instance of an application version
**Environment tier** — Web server environment or Worker environment

rows: Add or remove instances based on load

data.text: How ASP.NET Core Runs on Elastic Beanstalk
Elastic Beanstalk detects the ASP.NET Core app and runs it behind IIS or as a standalone process. You deploy the published output, and Elastic Beanstalk manages the rest.

data.title: No IIS knowledge required
data.text: Elastic Beanstalk abstracts IIS for ASP.NET Core. You deploy the app, and AWS runs the published output.

items.question: Do I need to manage EC2 instances directly?
items.answer: No. Elastic Beanstalk manages the EC2 instances for you, though you can still access them through the AWS console if needed.

items.question: Can I run multiple environments?
items.answer: Yes. You can have separate development, staging, and production environments under the same Elastic Beanstalk application.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Elastic Beanstalk is a managed host for web apps and APIs
You upload application versions; Elastic Beanstalk manages infrastructure
Your ASP.NET Core app runs as published output with platform-managed networking
data.takeaway: Elastic Beanstalk is the fastest way to move an ASP.NET Core project from localhost to a production URL on AWS.
